content.title: About
content.content: Iced tea with lemonade is a refreshing non‑alcoholic beverage that blends flavorful tea with a sweet hint of lemonade. It is usually made from black or green tea, sweetened with sugar or syrup, and combined with lemon juice, sometimes topped with sparkling water.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink is especially popular in summer and is often served over ice with a lemon wedge.
The tea‑lemonade combination originated in the United States in the early 20th century as an alternative to carbonated sodas.
Tea provides a mild dose of caffeine, while lemon juice adds vitamin C.
Variations may include mint, ginger, berries, or flavored syrups such as peach or strawberry.
Because it is easy to make at home, many people prepare it using bagged tea and ready‑made lemonade concentrate.

items.title: Antioxidants from tea
items.content: Black and green tea are rich in polyphenols, which help combat free radicals and support heart health.

items.title: Vitamin C from lemon
items.content: Lemon juice is a good source of vitamin C, which contributes to immune system function.

items.title: Mild hydration
items.content: The beverage provides water and electrolytes, aiding hydration especially in hot weather.

items.title: Gentle energy boost
items.content: Caffeine from tea offers a subtle energy lift without sharp blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Lemon juice can stimulate gastric secretions, helping with digestion.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Commercial versions often contain high amounts of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of tooth decay.

items.title: Caffeine
items.content: Tea’s caffeine may cause insomnia or jitteriness in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Lemon juice raises the drink’s acidity, which may irritate the stomach of people with gastritis or reflux.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to citrus fruits, which can trigger skin reactions or swelling.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the iced tea lemonade chilled, over ice, with a lemon slice. You can add fresh mint, berries, or a splash of ginger syrup for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared drink in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. Over longer storage the flavor may change and sugar can crystallize.
